title: Check yourself: walking a collection that changes

questions.stem: A price job runs on a single thread. It walks a HashMap of 5,000 SKUs with a for-each over keySet() and calls prices.put(sku, newPrice) for every SKU. For SKUs sold in packs it also stores a pack price under sku + "-pack". What happens?

options.text: It completes, since the pack keys are added by the only thread that touches the map
options.says: one thread is enough: storing the pack price adds a key, a structural change that the iterator's next step detects

options.text: It throws partway through, since storing a pack key adds a key that the map didn't have before
options.says: the pack key is new, so put increments modCount; the iterator's next step sees the difference and throws ConcurrentModificationException

options.text: It throws at its second step, since its first put already replaced a price, before any pack key was stored
options.says: put of a key that is already there only replaces a value, which is not counted as a structural change

options.text: It completes, and the walk also visits the pack keys added during it, since the iterator follows the map as it grows
options.says: a HashMap iterator does not carry on after a structural change; its next step throws

origin.section: A Fail-Fast Iterator Checks a Counter on Every Step, and One Thread Is Enough to Trip It

questions.stem: A unit test builds an ArrayList of refunds [r1, r2, r3, r4, r5], walks it with a for-each, and calls list.remove(r) for r4 when it reaches it. The test finishes without an exception. What did the loop do with r5?

options.text: It never examined r5, since the loop ended before the next step could look at the change
options.says: after the removal hasNext() compares index 4 with size 4 and returns false, so next() and its check never run

options.text: It examined r5 normally, since a walk that ends without an exception stayed in step with the list
options.says: no exception proves nothing: the check is only in next(), which never ran for r5

options.text: It examined r5 normally, since the check only exists to catch changes made by other threads
options.says: the check catches changes by the same thread too; here it simply never ran

options.text: It never examined r5, since a for-each over an ArrayList walks a copy taken when the loop began
options.says: an ArrayList iterator walks the live array by index; walking a copy is what a CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator does

origin.section: The Check Is Best-Effort: Some Changes Slip Past It

questions.stem: A config reload walks a CopyOnWriteArrayList of routes with an explicit Iterator and calls iterator.remove() on each route marked stale. The list holds 40 routes, 3 of them stale. What happens?

options.text: The stale routes are removed, since the iterator removes from the list it was created from
options.says: a CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator walks an array that never changes and does not support remove()

options.text: The call throws UnsupportedOperationException at the first stale route, since the iterator's array can't be changed
options.says: the iterator holds the array that was current when it was created; that array is never changed, so remove() throws UnsupportedOperationException

options.text: The call throws ConcurrentModificationException at the next step, since the removal changed the list during the walk
options.says: a CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator never throws ConcurrentModificationException

options.text: The stale routes stay in the list without an exception, since the iterator's remove() only drops them from the copy it walks
options.says: the remove() does not quietly change the copy; it throws UnsupportedOperationException

origin.section: A CopyOnWriteArrayList Iterator Walks the Array It Started With

questions.stem: Stock counts for 30 warehouses sit in a ConcurrentHashMap and total 50,000 units. One thread moves stock all day long: it adds the units to the destination first, then subtracts them from the source. A dashboard thread totals the counts with a for-each over values() every second. Which statement about the dashboard holds?

options.text: A total below 50,000 can't appear on it, since each move adds to the destination before it subtracts from the source
options.says: a walk is not a view of one moment; it can read the source after a subtraction and the destination before the matching addition

options.text: A total below 50,000 can appear on it, since the walk can read the source and the destination of one move at different moments
options.says: the walk reads keys at different moments, so it can add up a total that no state of the map ever had

options.text: An exception instead of a total can appear on it, since a move can change a source or a destination while the walk reads it
options.says: ConcurrentHashMap iterators are weakly consistent and never throw ConcurrentModificationException

options.text: A total the map never held can't appear on it, since the walk reads the map as it stood at the moment the walk began
options.says: a ConcurrentHashMap walk is not a snapshot; it may or may not reflect changes made after it started

origin.section: A ConcurrentHashMap Walk Never Throws, and It Is Not a Snapshot
